description: An oval diamond is the round brilliant stretched — the same facets, the same fire, carried along a longer path of light. The Dentelle setting was drawn so the prongs holding it read as lace arches connecting stone to stone rather than mechanical grips on the centre. The metalwork exists entirely in service of the oval's optical quality: it decorates the line without ever interrupting it, so the diamonds appear to float in a run of fine arches. Set in platinum, made to fit.
